title: [Inductor][NVGEMM] Match heuristic tiles per CTA
body:
Human commentary: Fixes a bug where 2-CTA kernels weren't considered.

AI-generated draft:

> ## Issue
>
> Fixes #196313
>
> ## Summary
>
> `nvMatmulHeuristics` reports tile M per CTA, while CUTLASS reports a pair-wide M tile for true 2-CTA kernels. Comparing those values directly prevented recommended dense 2-CTA kernels from entering NVGEMM autotuning.
>
> Normalize heuristic-matching keys using the implementation's `use_2cta_instrs` metadata, with a guarded design-metadata fallback for older kernels. The design flag alone is insufficient because block-scaled operators can set it for 1-CTA kernels. Supplemental configs continue to use raw design coordinates, preserving distinct 128-row and 256-row candidates.
>
> For example, a dense pair-wide `(256, 128, 2, 1)` design now matches the heuristic's per-CTA `(128, 128, 2, 1)` recommendation, while a block-scaled 1-CTA `(128, 128, 2, 1)` design remains unchanged.
>
> ## Checklist
>
> - [ ] Passes lint (`spin fixlint` is unavailable in this environment)
> - [x] Added regression tests
> - [x] Documentation is not applicable
> - [ ] B300 benchmarks were not rerun locally; reporter results are linked in #196313
>
> ## Tests
>
> The focused source-loaded filtering suite passed 6 tests covering dense 2-CTA normalization, block-scaled 1-CTA preservation, metadata fallback and absence, ordering, and supplemental raw-key collisions.
>
> `lintrunner -a --skip PYREFLY torch/_inductor/heuristics/template/nv_universal_gemm.py test/inductor/test_nv_universal_gemm.py` passed with no lint issues. Full `lintrunner -a` exited successfully but emitted unrelated repo-wide Pyrefly diagnostics because the refreshed worktree has no lintrunner initialization and the editable build targets an older checkout.
>
> B300 performance was not available locally; the issue contains the reporter's B300 timings for the same key correction.
>
> ## BC-breaking?
>
> No. This corrects internal matching of equivalent kernel metadata and preserves existing supplemental-key behavior.
>
> Authored with assistance from an AI coding agent.
